verdict.reasoning: Patient says, "I've been having this, blinding headache for a few days" and later clarifies onset was three days ago: "I woke up one morning with a headache, and that was three days ago."
Onset: "it just started all of a sudden. I woke up one morning with a headache"; Constant: "Kinda all the time... then I still have it, it's still there."

Severity: "I guess it's mostly, eight, and then it kinda comes down to maybe a five." Response to ibuprofen: "Doesn't really go away with Ibuprofen either... It gets a little bit better but like, doesn't go away."

Location: "it's kind of all over but, I feel like over my right eye, it's um bit, stronger." Positional/head movement: "Sometimes when I stand up, quickly I get a bit of a, stabbing pain. Um, or if I throw my head like, it I kind of feel like something is moving inside."

Photophobia: "lights definitely make me more sensitive. Like, um, I don't really, like strong lights." Visual disturbance: "yeah, vision I think, I get this, shooting light sometimes... just a bit of um, weird kind of vision."
Nausea without vomiting: Doctor asks about nausea/vomiting; patient replies, "Uh, no, feeling a bit sick, but no vomiting."

No focal neuro symptoms: To "Any tingling? Or numbness? Or weakness anywhere?" patient answers, "Um, no." No URTI/sinus: To "any cold symptoms, sore throat, sore ears, or pain over the sinuses? Any cough or flem?" patient says "No, no." No nosebleeds/hemoptysis: "Any, any nose bleeds, or coughing up any blood or anything?" – "No." No fever: "you haven't had a high temperature... Have you checked your temperature?" – patient: "I don't really feel, feverish or anything."

Sleep: Doctor asks, "are you able to fall asleep?" Patient: "yeah, I'm, sleeping well." Doctor: "Is it waking you up in the night-time?" Patient: "No, no, no. But I can wake up with it in the morning."

Impaired concentration and missed work: "I find it very hard to focus or, like I can't even go to work" and later describes work days: she worked from home day 1, took whole day off day 2, and stopped at midday day 3 — i.e., 1.5 days off in total.
Analgesia tried: "Doesn't really go away with Ibuprofen either, I try that" and later, "no apart from the Ibuprofen that I take, sometimes when, the headache gets really bad, nothing else."

When asked about other medical problems: patient says only, "I think I only had a, a pain, um, when I was younger but, no causes found and that went away, but that's, the only thing I know of," indicating no significant ongoing past medical history.
Family history: "my mum, suffers from, like she has migraines" and reiterated, "I know that my mum like, she has quite bad migraines, she's like, has the vomiting and everything."
OCP: Patient: "Um, just the pill." Doctor: "And when did you start that?" Patient: "Um, about a year ago."
Ibuprofen as needed: "Doesn't really go away with Ibuprofen either, I try that" and later, "no apart from the Ibuprofen that I take, sometimes when, the headache gets really bad, nothing else."
Allergies: Doctor asks, "any allergies to anything?" Patient: "No."

Lives alone: "Who do you live with at home?" – "Uh, just by myself." Non-smoker: "And do you smoke?" – "Uh, no." Alcohol: "How much in a normal week do you think?" – "Um, probably like, three , once a week" (≈3 drinks per week).
No illicit drugs: "And do you take any other drugs at all?" – "Um, no apart from the Ibuprofen... nothing else." No recent travel: "Have you been abroad recently at all?" – "No."

New severe headache: first time this bad – "it's obviously the first time you've had such a bad headache." Photophobia and visual disturbance present as per history. Doctor: "it, it, it could possibly be a migraine type headache. But, the fact it's still ongoing for three days, we probably should, book you into an appointment to get an examination," implying consideration of migraine vs secondary cause.

Doctor links OCP and migraine with aura: "when you have a, an examination with us, we'll check your blood pressure as well... because sometimes if we, if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill. If you've had these flashing lights, and things like that."

Suboptimal pain control evidenced by persistent high pain despite ibuprofen: "I've been having this, blinding headache"; "Doesn't really go away with Ibuprofen either... It gets a little bit better but like, doesn't go away" and severity 8/10 most of the time.
Limitation of work/ADLs: "I find it very hard to focus or, like I can't even go to work" and description of needing to take days off and stopping work mid-morning.

In-person exam plan: "we probably should, book you into an appointment to get an examination" and specifically, "we should do a neurological examination, look at the back of your eyes as well" and later, "when you have a, an examination with us, we'll check your blood pressure as well."

Medication plan: "I can prescribe you something, similar to Ibuprofen, but a bit stronger which you can take instead of Ibuprofen. And you can also take Paracetamol at the same time... take it with food." This supports a stronger NSAID + paracetamol and implies not co-using extra ibuprofen.

Red flag advice: "if in the meantime before your appointment your, headache is getting unbearable, getting worse or changing. Then , um, if it's that bad, then you should go to A and E and have an examination. Um, , you can call us for further advice on that." This covers worsening/intolerable pain and change in pattern as triggers for A&E.

OCP reassessment: "when you have a, an examination with us... because sometimes if we, if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill. If you've had these flashing lights, and things like that."

Contact/cancellation advice: "if it settles, in the meantime then, we can cancel that" (re appointment), and "if you're happy to book a, , appointment with us, with the support line, for us to do a full examination" and later, "you can call us for further advice on that."
